translations.answer: APEX uses phase-dependent foot-force and foot-velocity rewards to learn and demonstrate walking, running, hopping, skipping, and galloping on Cassie. This does not establish arbitrary humanoids, difficult terrain, or seamless gait switching; transfer requires renewed validation of phase, contact, torque, and fall protection.
translations.applicability.assumptions.0: The phase variable, foot-contact estimate, and low-level PD controller are stable and available.
translations.applicability.assumptions.1: Reward phases, actuator limits, and contact boundaries are revalidated on the target platform.
translations.applicability.controllers.0: Recurrent policy with joint PD control.
translations.applicability.environments.0: Periodic flat-ground gaits and simulation-to-real transfer.
translations.confidence_rationale: The paper and official code support periodic force/velocity reward composition and Cassie multi-gait demonstrations. Large-scale hardware success rates, cross-robot evidence, and difficult-terrain evidence are absent.
translations.evidence.0.locator: Figures 2–4, Tables I–II, and Sections III–V.
translations.evidence.0.note: Defines periodic reward composition and the policy, then reports simulated and hardware results for common Cassie gaits.
translations.evidence.0.title: Sim-to-Real Learning of All Common Bipedal Gaits via Periodic Reward Composition
translations.terms.1: Proportional-Derivative Control (比例-微分控制, PD Control)
translations.title: Can periodic reward composition teach a biped several common gaits?
